title: Fifty become five
hookLine: fifty prayers are given, Musa urges him to ask for less, and five remain with the reward of fifty (Bukhari)
tomorrow: "If he said it, it is true"

cards: Of everything that happened on the night of the ascent, what he carried home for his community to keep was a daily practice.
And according to Sahih al-Bukhari, it started out much bigger than the one Muslims keep today, and it changed size because of a conversation with Musa on the way down.
Today closes our week of sorrow and wonder: from Ta'if to the heavens, and back to the prayer mat. Fifty become five.

teach.b: Bukhari keeps it in reports from Abu Dharr and from Malik ibn Sa'sa'a. At the highest point of the ascent, Allah enjoins on him and his community fifty prayers a day. He accepts and starts back down.

teach.h: MUSA: YOUR PEOPLE CAN'T BEAR IT.
teach.b: He passes Musa, in the sixth heaven, and Musa asks: what were you commanded? Fifty prayers. And Musa, the prophet who led a whole people out of Egypt and through the wilderness, speaks from experience.
In Bukhari's words, roughly: your community won't be able to bear it. I have dealt with people before you. Go back and ask your Lord to lighten it.
So he goes back, and it is lightened. Down again past Musa, and Musa says the same thing: go back.
Back and forth, the reports say, until it is five. And Musa says, still too much, go back once more. Here the Prophet says something very human: I have asked my Lord until I feel ashamed.
I am content, and I accept.

teach.h: THEY ARE FIVE, AND THEY ARE FIFTY.
teach.b: Then the word comes: they are five, and they are fifty. My word does not change. So the number got smaller, and the weight didn't.
Look at who helped. Not an angel, but Musa, an older prophet who had led a difficult people and knew what daily life does to good intentions.
And look at the week behind us: a man refused at Ta'if, comforted with grapes, offered revenge and refusing it, carried to Jerusalem, welcomed at every heaven.
What he brings back down is five times a day.

how: Muslims pray the five daily prayers, salah, at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night, and the story of how fifty became five is taught with the Mi'raj.

o: the angel who carried the fifty prayers down
Abraham, who waits in the seventh heaven
Moses, who urged him to ask for fewer prayers

games.q: you're coming down with fifty daily prayers. an older prophet stops you and says your people won't bear it. what do you do?
o: go on down; the command is the command.
go back and ask your Lord to lighten it.
ask him to go and ask for you.
games.why: he went back again and again, until five remained, with the reward of fifty.

practice: If you pray, picture where each of today's five prayers will fit, dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night, naming the place and the moment for each.
If you don't, choose five moments to stop for one breath, morning, noon, afternoon, evening and before sleep, and see each one now, in order. Small, fixed, five.

wordCard.voice: Musa. In the sixth heaven he told the Prophet to ask again and again, until fifty prayers became five, with the weight of fifty still kept. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the set prayer, offered five times a day.

carryVoice: Your line: five, weighing fifty. Small enough to keep, heavy enough to matter. A week complete, and day seven hundred fifty-six.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (Abu Dharr: fifty prayers enjoined; Musa urges him to go back; 'they are five and they are fifty; the word does not change with Me')
Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a: Musa says he has dealt with people before; 'I have asked my Lord until I feel ashamed; I am content and I accept')
